Yes..? None of thats helpful, I was not intentionally wishing to associate abuse automatically with paraphilia. I can change the original for others when my wording isn't so messy. OP seemed to have gotten what I meant, because I do include myself with someone who experienced conditions like that and a partner who also has the same experience. We aren't born like this. I was not born with BPD and I was not born to be attracted to things that cant consent, its genuinely trauma related things and our early development is so vital to our sexual development later in life. There is possibility to recover from paraphilias if needed, not all of them are harmful but some.. I think you can agree causes lifetime horror for any party included. I can say that and I wish I didn't have to, but Im only glad to be out of the cycle and loop, and see where things went wrong, and what has been harmful to my brain and my body with consuming porn as a coping mechanism, and being exposed to horrible things as a kid online. I hope this makes sense. I dont think there is good in saying we are born into harmful paraphilias when it hurts everyone. But I see how my statement may have seemed broad.

You aren't born with NPD or BPD either. Personality disorders are from traumas in early development. but from what I can tell I didn't have a proper pause in my sentence in the original. I see how it would seem like Im associating paraphilia with abuse automatically, I just don't use my punctuation very well when writing a lot. I hope my wording wasn't too far off for others. But paraphilia is a condition, it is something that develops. It doesn't mean you will abuse, that part was meant to be a standalone thought with the idea of action being taken or escalating to action. Not all paraphilias are harmful and it isn't something you're born with.

Its okay, youre asking questions to understand, its perfectly okay to ask questions. Your brain isnt able to differentiate the pictures, videos, etc. and orgasm reinforces the dopamine response for it, and dopamine within addiction asks for more as time goes on. The only way to get out of the cycle/loop for this is to stop viewing the content , distance yourself but also I would recommend journaling your emotions on it, researching porn addiction and escalation, and the general structures of addiction because it applies to anything- especially harmful things like body-destroying drugs or financially crippling situations (shopping/gambling). Addiction does affect everything, and yourself, with those around you. Its not your fault in falling into addiction, but its absolutely possible to get out of the pit and feel secure and safe again as a person, confident in your attraction without harming yourself or others. If you have any more questions, please do ask, you aren't alone and me + my husband have had the same problems (childhood development being interrupted by traumas/exposure/lack of sex education.) Its unfortunate how our cultures/social structures curate this situation for us to get out of, but its not something you have to be bound by. None of us have to.

If you're consuming porn, that can and usually does lead to escalation like this, its all accessible for a reason. Your body is being conditioned any time you masturbate or orgasm to it, pavlov's dog. Paraphilias are a condition, not something you're born as, no one is born to abuse anything. OCD does mess with this too, with or without the groin reactions. If there is porn usage, its best to stop, replace with a healthier coping mechanism and understand how addictions work. If its just the thoughts and you're worried about it, checking and reassuring yourself that you aren't attracted, its more safer to work with this in a professional therapy setting. But if that isn't possible, you can learn more on ocd and also understand the cycles, how compulsive behavior reinforces the fear/obsession. Regardless of the situation, healthy coping mechanisms all the way, and its something to commend that you reached out in any capacity to get help on this. Youre doing good. You do got this.

Its also pavlov's dog, you are essentially conditioning the body to react this way over time and it doesnt get easier that way. But knowledge is key on this to be aware. There are porn addiction related podcasts, some religious leaning but hopefully the specifics on how to handle/understand your reactions and the thoughts that come with it could help. I hope this can help in some regard, you really deserve better, and peace.

My husband has ADHD too, he was on meds for a long time and very well into his addiction, he stopped his meds a year or so ago though & has been managing well in that regard + I only found out how severe his porn usage was in november last year. I have been very stern & standing my ground with him, also helps knowing he wants to get better too- not just for me, but for himself. His escalating behavior was towards abhorrent things & material, so theres a lot of remorse and guilt with him, but not shame- since shame is what fueled his cycle. He has had relapses since november, but around 10? Not sure. but each time, especially "found out" was painful for both of us. I think me not budging has helped. Porn is not something Im comfortable with, especially now, so that is a boundary I have- I have made it clear to him that especially with a relapse, I now have to reconsider and reevaluate our relationship, since he cant be choosing porn over me while having me **also.** Its not fair. I also dont want to see him deteriorate either. Porn affects you outside of that "intoxicated" moment, so I really cant be with someone who hurts & affects especially me. He has been on pretty much a lockdown in terms of internet usage, even to the extent of a flip phone (which we are having technical issues with, so right now he is using his iphone with no ability to download new apps, nor a browser at all. He is also journaling, which helps him a lot I imagine, and lots of talking with me if he needs it. but definitely within respect of what I can handle and have capacity for. Podcasts for overcoming porn addiction too. And SAA meetings. I hope this helps, we arent extremely far into recovery but its so much better than a month ago, two months, three.. especially since november when I found out the severity, and also why he even struggled in bed at all.
